liarCellCount.paragraph: For the record, the liar cells file is settled. My note gave the data two doors: poison, or a rounding error, and it picked the second. A liar barely moves the clock. The study covered ten study days from April 22 to June 28, and the cost fell between 0% and about 3% per ten liar cells, which is thin either way. The best files are the ones I can stop writing in.

clueShare4.paragraph: Every fresh look at fours gives the same reading, with the data showing that each extra four in ten numbers adds about 13% to your time, likely between 7% and 19%. This range has barely moved since Jul 18, with the number reading the same and the file staying open a while longer. My note asked how big the four costs, not whether it exists, and now the focus is on telling the fours apart from the boards around them.

wormholePairCount.paragraph: The wormholes band is widening when it should be narrowing, with the width up 878% in this window. I continue to collect data. I predicted that splitting one number across two places would slow the reading down, and it does: ten wormhole pairs add about 50% to your time, likely between 25% and 78%. I haven’t retracted the hypothesis, but it’s on notice.

patternMoves.paragraph: Back into the pattern reasoning file, I found that the parked estimate moved from about 11% per ten pattern deductions on Jul 13 to now about 44%. The cost comes to roughly the same 44% per ten pattern deductions. The band for this estimate runs from 35% to 53%. I wrote that a practiced read should cost seconds, not tens of seconds, and the data agree: the effect is real but small. I don’t like surprises in closed drawers.

sonarCellCount.paragraph: I closed the sonar file, and it moved while I wasn’t looking. The model puts the change at about 107% per ten sonar cells, which falls inside the range of 73% to 149%. The parked estimate moved as well: it was about 37% per ten sonar cells on Jul 2, and now it reads 107%. A number that moves on its own has my full attention.

mysteryCellCount.paragraph: I opened the mystery cells file expecting progress and found the opposite. The charge per ten mystery cells reads between 0% and about 3%, a range that has widened by 29% since Jul 2. I wrote that missing information has a price. I measured it, and the price is close to free. Instruments drift, so do estimates. The notebook is the record.

clueShare2.paragraph: In two study days, the answer for twos remains the same as hypothesized: a two should read almost as fast as a one. The range puts it slightly above that, and I still cannot distinguish the twos from the boards they appear on. Since July 18, the range has narrowed by 27%. Each additional two in ten numbers adds about 5%, likely between 3% and 7%. The same answer came back again, and I am listening.

compassCellCount.paragraph: The compass question remains open, where I left it. My current estimate is about 65% per ten compass cells, likely between 36% and 100%, a range that has not moved. I wrote that I couldn’t tell whether players read the arrow fast or stopped to puzzle over it, and so far, neither can the model. The file stays open, and so does the question.
